title: Disentangled Ontology Embedding for Zero-shot Learning

problem.claim: The work addresses augmenting zero-shot learning with knowledge graphs or ontologies.

gap.claim: Existing KG-based zero-shot learning methods neglect the intrinsic complexity of inter-class relationships, including relationships expressed across different semantic aspects.

contributions.claim: Disentangled ontology embeddings guided by ontology properties are proposed to capture and use fine-grained class relationships across different aspects.
DOZSL is introduced as a zero-shot learning framework with generative-model and graph-propagation-model solutions for using disentangled ontology embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluations on five benchmarks covering zero-shot image classification and zero-shot knowledge graph completion.
The authors report that DOZSL often outperforms the state of the art.
The authors report component verification through ablation studies and case studies.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graphs and ontologies are used to augment zero-shot learning.
Existing methods overlook the complexity and multiple semantic aspects of inter-class relationships.
The paper proposes ontology-property-guided disentangled ontology embeddings.
DOZSL provides generative and graph-propagation solutions for using those embeddings.
The framework is evaluated across five benchmarks and is reported to perform better than the state of the art in many cases.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or details of the ablation and case studies.
The abstract does not describe the ontology properties, model architectures, or training procedures.
